title: Meta Boosts Bet on AI With Spending Outlook, New Stock Class

summary: Meta Platforms boosted its capital spending outlook and announced plans for a new class of nonvoting stock, escalating its already-stratospheric bet on artificial intelligence. Capital expenditures will be $135 billion to $145 billion in 2026, the social-media giant said during its quarterly earnings report Wednesday, raising the bottom end of the range from $130 billion. The new class of shares, meanwhile, will be distributed to existing investors through a stock dividend. Holders will get one share of the new stock in what will essentially be a two-for-one stock split, Meta said. It expects trading of the new shares to begin in January. Bloomberg Tech Host Ed Ludlow joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss.  He speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Make Your Move Summit (Podcast)
title_cn: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Make Your Move Summit (Podcast)
summary:
US small business optimism fell to a three-month low in September as economic expectations dimmed and a smaller share of firms indicated it was a good time to expand. The net share of owners who expect business conditions to improve declined 4 percentage points to a four-month low of 6%. Despite a falling economic sentiment, JPMorganChase says most small business owners view their own business outlook in a positive light, highlighting the resiliency of small businesses. Bloomberg Businessweek is live from the Chase Make Your Move Summit in Atlanta discussing the future of small businesses in America.

On today's episode:

Stevie Baron, CEO Chase for Business
Katie Kirkpatrick, President & CEO of the Metro Atlanta Chamber
Leslie Wims Morris, CEO, Chase Auto
Reggie Washington, Restaurateur at SONAT Hospitality Group & Southern National Restaurant (Source: Bloomberg)
